modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a per-inlet-channel matrix with physical fan/rotor identity, raw RPM/unit/status/threshold, PWM/temperature context and UI display/timestamp; evaluate expected versus observed under the owner cooling curve/tolerances.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact population/mapping and operating-context plausibility while replacing truncated/insecure generic reads and log clearing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One tach value or UI screenshot cannot cover FAN1..N, thresholds or correct inlet-channel association; every expected sensor is in the denominator and needs context.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: RPM varies dynamically with fan policy, temperature and dual-rotor topology. Snapshot tolerances and whether INLET denotes a rotor/channel must come from the platform spec.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, WebUI Procedure and Criteria consistently target inlet tach readings/thresholds. Exact fan-channel mapping and operating context are required project inputs rather than source contradictions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Mapping/spec/UI prerequisites gate execution, while the static review is complete and no source-integrity stop exists.

review_improvement: Defines the full inlet tach denominator and couples each reading to physical fan identity and cooling context instead of treating a literal family-name read as coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A tach value is only meaningful when tied to the correct rotor/channel and current PWM/thermal demand. A nonzero RPM can still be wrong for the commanded duty, while zero may be valid only for a deliberately stopped/redundant channel defined by the spec. Inlet and outlet labels may describe dual rotors, so their records must remain distinct. UI and raw values should be sampled close in time because control loops can change speed between reads; an unexplained mismatch is preserved rather than retried away.
